design: The design spec for the whole project is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/spec/mcp/proposal-mcp.qmd (fetch it with curl if you need it).

spec.design: files to add/change, exported interfaces, zod schemas for every capability's input and output, MCP tool and REST route for each, upstream calls with example URLs and fixture files to record

implement: Run npm ci first in a fresh worktree. Record fixtures by fetching the upstream URLs once with curl into test/fixtures/; tests must not use the network.

lenses.code: CODE review. Correctness against the issue spec and its acceptance criteria; tests that would actually catch a regression (fixtures, no network); the one-capability-two-transports rule (no logic in transports/); deep modules with clear seams; type safety; dead code; dependency choices against AGENTS.md. The spec and the code must agree: rules, interfaces and example snippets in the spec match what the code does, because later issues copy the spec (a stale spec is "major").
lenses.ux: AGENT + DEVELOPER UX review. Tool names; descriptions that say what the tool answers and when to use another tool instead; input/output schema clarity and defaults; error messages an agent can act on; result size (≤ ~8 KB text) and pagination; provenance on every result; REST paths, query params and OpenAPI quality; README/connection instructions for a first-time user.
lenses.security: SECURITY review. SSRF (no capability fetches a caller-supplied URL or host); input validation and bounds; secret handling (code, fixtures, logs, CI); fork-PR CI safety (no secrets on pull_request, no pull_request_target); Host/Origin allowlist; rate limiting; that nothing non-public can be returned.
